Maintenance Report — MNT-0021-001

Asset: WELL-0021 (SW-23 Well 021, T350, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: flowline Work started: 11 Nov 2022 08:00 · Finished: 11 Nov 2022 18:00 · Well stopped for this job: 10 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Brian Coleman, Megan Ward · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0021-0004 on 2022-11-10 Report written: 13 Nov 2022

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0021-0004 at 14:15 on 2022-11-10 found crude oil on the pad: about 4.5% of the pad area, estimated 2.6 bbl. The inspector noted: "Dark staining on pad." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 3.3 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Thread fatigue from pump jack vibration.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 291 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 233 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 1.6 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0021-001 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.2% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0021-007

Asset: WELL-0021 (SW-23 Well 021, T350, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: downhole pump Work started: 29 Oct 2023 08:00 · Finished: 15 Nov 2023 12:00 · Well stopped for this job: 412 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Megan Ward, Brian Coleman Triggered by: inspection INS-0021-0054 on 2023-10-26 Report written: 17 Nov 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the wellhead was cold and the pump jack was straining with a heavy, uneven load. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0021-0054 showed the wellhead at 27.8 °C with the air at 17.6 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The downhole pump was stuck, most likely from sand or scale. The company workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 15 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

Sand and scale build-up in the pump barrel.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rods and the insert pump.
  3. Inspected the pump: sand in the barrel and a worn plunger.
  4. Ran in a new insert pump.
  5. Re-spaced the pump and hung the rods back on.

Summary of the fix: pulled and replaced downhole pump.

Testing and return to service

Pump test confirmed fluid to surface and the wellhead warmed back to normal. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0021-014

Asset: WELL-0021 (SW-23 Well 021, T350, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 30 Aug 2024 08:00 · Finished: 10 Sep 2024 09:00 · Well stopped for this job: 265 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Daniel Foster, Megan Ward · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0021-0098 on 2024-08-29 Report written: 11 Sep 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the motor breaker kept tripping and the pump jack would not run. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0021-0098 showed the wellhead at 43.0 °C with the air at 34.3 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 9 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

Moisture got into the motor terminal box and damaged the windings.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Maintenance Report — MNT-0021-015

Asset: WELL-0021 (SW-23 Well 021, T350, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 17 Nov 2024 08:00 · Finished: 26 Nov 2024 08:00 · Well stopped for this job: 216 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Brian Coleman · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0021-0109 on 2024-11-14 Report written: 28 Nov 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that oil was dripping from the gearbox onto the pump jack base. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0021-0109 showed the wellhead at 21.8 °C with the air at 12.1 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass. The well stayed shut in for about 7 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Root cause

Seal wear, made worse by heat and a low oil level.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Drained the gearbox oil into a closed container.
  2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
  3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
  4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Summary of the fix: replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 1 hour and checked both shafts for leaks: none found. The well was returned to production.

Waste

Maintenance Report — MNT-0021-032

Asset: WELL-0021 (SW-23 Well 021, T350, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 04 Jul 2026 08:00 · Finished: 08 Jul 2026 01:00 · Well stopped for this job: 89 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Brian Coleman, Daniel Foster Triggered by: inspection INS-0021-0193 on 2026-07-02 Report written: 10 Jul 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that oil was dripping from the gearbox onto the pump jack base. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0021-0193 showed the wellhead at 37.1 °C with the air at 34.5 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass. The well stayed shut in for about 2 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

A hardened output shaft seal after years of service.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Drained the gearbox oil into a closed container.
  2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
  3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
  4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Summary of the fix: replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 1 hour and checked both shafts for leaks: none found. The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Used gear oil and oily pads sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0021-032 (WS-06).
